display_name: Lafage Tessellae Old Vines, Côtes du Roussillon
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Old vines averaging 80 years old cling to black schist slopes in Roussillon's Agly Valley, where low yields from gnarled Grenache, Carignan, and Syrah roots deliver dense, spicy reds. Lafage's Tessellae skips oak aging to let that schist-driven earthiness shine through licorice and black olive notes. Berliner Wine Trophy silvers across vintages confirm its reliability.",
  "wine_summary": "Lafage crafts Tessellae from unirrigated old-vine parcels across 12 hectares in Côtes du Roussillon, blending the appellation's core grapes—Grenache, Carignan, Syrah—under sustainable farming that preserves biodiversity on steep, wind-swept sites. This approach sets Lafage apart in a region racing toward organic certification, producing wines that punch above entry-level pricing without chasing high-alcohol trends. The result matters because it revives Roussillon's rustic heritage amid Languedoc's polished exports.",
  "terroir_expression": "Black schist soils—crumbled metamorphic rock rich in iron and magnesium—force roots deep into fractured bedrock, yielding wines with graphite minerality and compressed black fruit that unfolds into peppery persistence. Mediterranean climate with hot days cooled by Tramontane winds prevents overripening, preserving Carignan's bloody iron edge and Grenache's wild herb garrigue amid Syrah's smoke. That geology translates to a taut, soil-stained structure avoiding flabby jam.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested grapes undergo partial whole-cluster fermentation in concrete tanks, a technique that extracts gentler tannins via intracellular breakdown (carbonic maceration's light touch) while building color from free-run juice. No oak aging keeps the focus on fruit purity and terroir snap; short macerations (10-15 days) for each variety ensure balance before blending. These choices amplify old-vine concentration without masking schist's raw pulse.",
  "food_pairing": "BBQ brisket sliced thick—smoky char meets the wine's iron-laced Carignan and licorice grip for a Texas pitmaster match. Lamb merguez sausages with harissa—spice amplifies Syrah's pepper while schist earth tempers heat. Seared duck breast with cherry gastrique—tart fruit echoes Grenache's core, tannins cut fat cleanly. Nashville hot chicken tenders—the vinegar brine lifts acidity against cayenne burn, turning heat into harmony. Veal osso buco with gremolata—marrow richness yields to grippy structure, herbs mirroring garrigue lift.",
  "comparable_wines": "Guigal Côtes du Rhône — shared Grenache-Syrah-Carignan blend delivers similar spicy black fruit at everyday prices, though less schist focus. Clos des Paulilles Côtes du Roussillon Villages — neighboring old-vine intensity with more Mourvèdre-driven meatiness. Mas Amiel Old Vines — Roussillon peer with comparable schist rusticity but bolder alcohol.",
  "style_profile": "Grenache-Carignan-Syrah blend of medium-full body with rustic tannins and smoky garrigue thrust",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink NV and 2012 now; 2018 holds to 2026 with cool, dark storage at 55°F. Earlier vintages like 2011 peak soon—avoid heat swings that dull fruit.",
  "value_assessment": "20-25 CAD at LCBO shelves. Beats Guigal Côtes du Rhône or Paul Jaboulet Parallèle 45 at this price for old-vine depth and silver medals. Buy multiples—terroir punch crushes generic blends.",
  "market_position": "Bistro sommeliers stock it for by-the-glass pours targeting value seekers who want Roussillon without sticker shock. Retail hits everyday tables of home cooks exploring southern France. Skip collectors; it's for weeknight rotisseries, not auctions.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you demand polished New World fruit—schist austerity bites back early, demanding food. Old vines reward patient sippers with layering most dismiss as rustic. Priorat fans grab it for half the cost and similar tension.",
